business.title: Surgical technique for correction of sagittal translation using V-shaped rod repositioning and lifting reduction in ankylosing spondylitis kyphosis
business.description: A total of 29 patients with severe kyphosis deformity secondary to ankylosing spondylitis underwent posterior spinal osteotomy from October 2017 to April 2023, with intraoperative ST occurring in 7 cases. The primary surgical modification involved the application of V-shaped cobalt-chromium-molybdenum (CoCrMo) alloy rod and changing its place position in the pedicle screws for create displacement between rod and screw, subsequent locking of the screw facilitated a lifting reduction, ensuring accurate alignment and minimizing vertebral displacement. Clinical and radiographic data were collected for all 29 patients. Patient-Reported Outcome were assessed using Oswestry disability index(ODI) and the Scoliosis Research Society-22 (SRS-22) questionnaire for comparative analysis in addition. A total of 29 patients successfully underwent surgery. There were no significant differences in general characteristics between the 7 patients who experienced ST and the 22 patients who did not. Both groups showed significant improvements in sagittal alignment postoperatively, though no significant differences were observed between them. In the ST group, the global kyphosis (GK) improved from 88.3° ± 15.0 to 28.9° ± 20.7, Pelvic tilt(PT) decreased from 34.5°± 20.0 to 18.5° ± 12.8,while in the non-ST group, GK improved from 86.6° ± 28.1 to 30.9° ± 23.0, PT improved from 34.3° ± 15.5 to 26.1° ± 12.5. STs were corrected from 5.4mm ± 1.3 to 1.0mm ± 1.3, with no patients experienced neurological complications postoperatively. ODI improved from 42.6 ± 15.2 to 16.3 ± 7.2 in the ST group, and from 52.5 ± 12.6 to 22.6 ± 11.7 in the non-ST group. SRS-22 scores improved from 10.9±1.7 to 13.8±1.7 in the ST group, and from 10.3±2.6 to 13.9±1.9 in the non-ST group, both improved significantly. The novel surgical technique, utilizing V-shaped CoCrMo rod repositioning within the pedicle screw construct and subsequent lifting reduction, is a safe and effective approach for correcting ST in patients with kyphosis deformity secondary to ankylosing spondylitis.

science.title: High-speed FPGA implementation of the CORDIC algorithm using carry lookahead adders
science.description: This paper presents an efficient hardware architecture for sine and cosine generation using the CORDIC (Coordinate Rotation Digital Computer) algorithm. The design employs a pipelined scale-free CORDIC datapath integrated with a carry look-ahead adder (CLA) to reduce critical path delay and improve computational speed compared to conventional ripple-carry adder (RCA) implementations. To achieve an optimal balance between performance and hardware cost, hybrid CLA–RCA configurations are introduced, where CLAs are selectively used in timing-critical stages while RCAs are retained in non-critical paths. Furthermore, mutually exclusive micro-rotation techniques are utilized to reduce the number of iterations and eliminate the need for scale-factor compensation, thereby enhancing efficiency. The proposed architecture is implemented and synthesized on both FPGA and ASIC platforms to validate its performance and portability. FPGA implementation on Xilinx Artix-7 confirms accurate sine and cosine outputs with low power consumption of 0.175W, while a standard-cell ASIC realization on the open SkyWater 130 nm (Sky130) PDK using the Yosys–OpenROAD flow further demonstrates a core area of $$0.88 \textrm{mm}^{2}$$, an achievable clock frequency of $$32 \textrm{MHz}$$, and a total power of $$10.2 \textrm{mW}$$, confirming successful timing closure with zero violations across all sign-off corners.

science.title: The effect of two distinct viral-enriched inocula on the immune response and chemical cues of honey bee pupae
science.description: The Varroa destructor (Varroa) and its vectored viruses are major drivers of honey bee (Apis mellifera) colony losses. Hygienic behavior, activated by olfactory cues from diseased brood, enables bees to cope with some pests and pathogens. In this study, we evaluated the effect of viral inoculation with varying doses of either deformed wing virus (DWV) B-A recombinant- or Israeli acute paralysis virus (IAPV) -enriched inoculum on pupal volatiles and immune response, independently of Varroa. Both inocula came from biological material commonly containing background levels of both viruses. Five days post-treatment, volatile profiles, viral loads, and expression of seven immune genes were assessed. IAPV-enriched inoculum caused dose-dependent mortality (up to 60%), while DWV-enriched inoculum caused limited mortality. All pupae injected with DWV-enriched inoculum exhibited high viral RNA levels of both DWV and IAPV, resulting in a DWV + IAPV co-infection, whereas pupae injected with the IAPV-enriched inoculum displayed high IAPV and dose-dependent DWV. Expression of immune genes was lower in pupae injected with IAPV-enriched inoculum-and lower immune gene expression than in the DWV+IAPV co-infected pupae, suggesting IAPV suppresses the immunity. Volatile profile of virus-injected pupae differed from controls. The ultimate consequence of such differences might lead to virus specific hygienic responses.
